evidence.quote: The flowers appear during August, September and October. Male and female plants are separate... The orange-brown fruits are borne during February, March and April.

harvestMonths.notes: Flowering Aug-Oct (months [8,9,10] for reference only, not the harvested product); fruit borne Feb-Apr.

evidence.quote: In southern Africa flowering usually occurs in August–December, and fruits mature in February–May.
evidence.doc: PROTA (Plant Resources of Tropical Africa) - Phoenix reclinata, via Pl@ntUse mirror

harvestMonths.notes: Broader southern-Africa regional figure, overlapping with but slightly wider than the PZA South-Africa-specific window (extends flowering to December and fruiting to May).

yearsToFirstCrop.notes: PROTA states 'a coppice shoot is estimated to need 6-8 years of growth before it can be tapped' for palm wine - this is time-to-wine-tapping-readiness of a coppice shoot, NOT age to first fruiting/fruit crop, so it was deliberately excluded from this field rather than misapplied.

chillUnits.notes: Tropical/subtropical palm; no source states a chilling requirement or its explicit absence.

evidence.quote: Male and female plants are separate.

pollination.notes: Corroborated by PROTA's structural description: 'Dioecious, usually clustering, rarely solitary tree up to 15 m tall...' (https://uses.plantnet-project.org/en/Phoenix_reclinata_(PROTA)). Both sources independently and directly confirm dioecy (separate male and female plants), which maps cleanly onto the schema's 'separate-male-female-plants' category.

gaps: yearsToFirstCrop / yearsToFullBearing / yieldKgPerTreeMature / chillUnits: not found in PZA, PROTA (Pl@ntUse mirror) or ICRAF Agroforestree Database for this species; PROTA's only age-related figure (6-8 years for a coppice shoot to be ready for wine-tapping) is for a different purpose (tapping, not fruit-bearing) and was explicitly not used for yearsToFirstCrop.
